Is there any way to find out, what's happening?

events.body_html: You really need to show all the lines between where you create the shared_ptr and where your program crashes. And indicate exactly what happens within any functions that you call. Chances are that in your conversion process, you may have called delete on the shared_ptr's raw pointer. Or you may have undefined behavior / heap corruption due to a buffer overrun somewhere. It's very difficult to tell based on the scant information you have provided thus far.
@paddy Well, I've tried to provide more code - if you need more information, I'll fill it in.

The error messages smell like a memory corruption error, which is notoriously hard to track down. You need to search for out-of-bounds accesses in a part of the code unrelated to the part that's giving you the errors.
Is that the very first error reported by valgrind memcheck?
@MarkRansom Do you think, it's possible to find it with some Valgrind flag?
I highly recommend adding the compiler flag -fsanitize=address and running it again
@xaxxon Thank you! I've tried it and appended the output into the question.
@paddy I've added additional info into my question.
@MarkRansom Could the newly added log from AddressSanitizer help you?

It seems something is overwriting memory that belongs to best_params. My next step would be to run under gdb. Put a breakpoint right after best_params is initialized. When you get there, set hardware watchpoints (watch command) on best_params itself and also on the memory at which it points. continue, then each time a hardware watchpoint trigger, look at whether it makes sense for the calling code to be modifying best_params or its shared block.
